news.title: Democrat Scott Colom seals historic win in Mississippi Senate race
news.summary: Colom is the first black person from the southern state elected to the US Senate in over 140 years.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Democrat Scott Colom seals historic win in Mississippi Senate race
news.summaryTr: Colom is the first black person from the southern state elected to the US Senate in over 140 years.
news.articleText: Democrat Scott Colom seals historic win in Mississippi Senate race - Published Democrat Scott Colom has won the US Senate race in Mississippi, delivering a shock victory for the party in a deeply conservative state that has elected Republicans for decades. Colom's victory makes him the first black person from Mississippi to be elected to the US Senate in more than 140 years. Fewer than five thousand votes out of nearly a million counted separated him from his Republican opponent, the incumbent Cindy Hyde-Smith. The result means the Democrats will hold 55 seats in the 100-member Senate, with a knife-edge race in Alaska still to be called. Colom, 43, won with 49.2% of the vote, while Hyde-Smith received 48.7% and an independent candidate got 2.1%, according to figures from CBS. Hyde-Smith congratulated Colom in a video posted on X on Wednesday evening and wished him well. "While this was not the outcome we worked for or hoped for, I respect the decision of Mississippi voters," she said. Colom offered a victory speech on the campus of Tougaloo College, met by hundreds of cheering supporters standing side-by-side under the night sky. Excitement filled the air as he thanked them for the support over the days of waiting for a result since the 4 November election. "They did not believe a moment like this was possible, but I kept the faith," Colom said. "It's not something that I did y'all," he continued. "It's something we did." "In Mississippi, it's local people that make the difference." Dozens of people were gathered at the Mississippi HQ of the National Association for the Advancement of Colored People (NAACP) in Jackson on Wednesday when Colom's victory was announced. The room burst into deafening applause and cheers. "This is an amazing result," said Leon Russell, chairman of the NAACP board. "This is purely the work of particularly the black community," he continued. "There was not a whole lot of money, but there was a whole lot of organising. "This is a historic election." Across the room, filled with people embracing, Amber Thomas sat, revelling in the victory. "When you fight, you win," Thomas said. "Right now, I am overwhelmed with joy." The result wipes away a Republican winning streak in the Magnolia State that dates back to 1982. The contest was never expected to be this close, with Hyde-Smith running for re-election in a state that President Donald Trump won in the 2024 election by more than 22 points. But Democrats have scored a series of major wins in these midterm elections, taking control of both the US House of Representatives and the Senate. The party flipped Senate seats in Republican strongholds, including Texas, South Carolina, Kansas and Iowa. Polls suggest this was due in large part to voter frustrations with the economy and the Iran war under President Trump. Colom appeared to a ride a national wave of resentment against Republicans. Voter backlash against Trump's Republican party has been driven in large part by economic woes, blamed on his administration's tariffs and war with Iran, according to exit polls. Colom, a local prosecutor, used the national mood to his advantage, highlighting his opponent's support for Trump's tariffs and giving her the nickname "Cindy High Prices". The Democrat campaigned aggressively, visiting all of Mississippi's 82 counties. Hyde-Smith's campaign assailed Colom as a puppet of billionaire liberal donor George Soros, whose family has helped fund the Democrat's political campaigns. The 67-year-old Republican was criticised for a lack of public appearances.

news.titleTr: Israeli strike on Nasser Hospital kills at least six, Gaza civil defence agency says
news.summaryTr: The strike hit the surgery department of the hospital in Khan Younis, wounding at least 20 people and causing extensive damage, a spokesperson says.
news.articleText: Israeli strike on Nasser Hospital kills at least six, Gaza civil defence agency says - Published At least six people have been killed after an Israeli airstrike hit a building at Nasser Hospital in southern Gaza, an official from the Hamas-run civil defence agency has said. The strike hit the surgery department of the hospital in Khan Younis, wounding at least 20 people and causing extensive damage, spokesperson Mahmoud Basal told news agency AFP. A surgeon is reported to be among those who were killed during the strike early on Thursday. There has been no immediate response from the Israeli military. The BBC has contacted the Israel Defense Forces for comment. The BBC is prevented by Israel from reporting independently from inside the Gaza Strip, and is unable to verify details of the incident. Recovery work is carried out by the Civil Defence in Gaza, which operates under the Hamas-run interior ministry. Its efforts have been supported by the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC). Nasser Hospital, the largest in southern Gaza, was hit by a double Israeli strike in August 2025, which killed at least 20 people, including journalists and health workers. Israeli strikes on Gaza have continued despite a ceasefire agreement in October last year. More than 1,600 people have been killed since then, according to Gaza's Hamas-run health ministry, whose figures are considered reliable by the UN. Israel and Hamas have accused each other of violating the ceasefire. The humanitarian crisis in Gaza has also worsened from recent heavy rains that reportedly flooded tens of thousands of tents that were housing displaced families. The Gaza war was triggered by the Hamas-led attack on southern Israel on 7 October 2023, when about 1,200 people were killed and 251 others were taken hostage. Since then, more than 74,645 people have been killed in Gaza, the health ministry says.

news.summary: The 17-year-old's mum has joked that he is "grounded for life" and "never leaving the house again".

news.titleTr: Australian teen missing in bush for six days rescued alive
news.summaryTr: The 17-year-old's mum has joked that he is "grounded for life" and "never leaving the house again".
news.articleText: Australian teen missing in bush for six days rescued alive - Published A teenager missing for six days in dense Australian bushland has been found alive. William, whose surname has not been released, disappeared last Friday while on a camping trip with a friend in bushland about 180km (112 miles) east of Melbourne, Victoria. Extremely cold overnight temperatures had left authorities concerned for the 17-year-old's welfare. Police dogs, divers and helicopters had been involved in the search. He was located on Friday morning and reunited with his relieved family, who said he was uninjured but "grounded for life". Rescuers winched William to safety, and fed him a doughnut and a bottle of water, before he was taken to hospital for a check up. The boy's mother, Elizabeth Barkley, told reporters the teenager had "only a few scratches" and seemed fit and healthy. "He's doing fine, everything seems to be fine, he's in perfect health," she added. "He just stayed in one spot and waited to be rescued and I'm just over the moon he's alive." Joking, she added: "He's never leaving the house again." Police have said officers were emotional to have found the teen alive. "It doesn't happen all the time," Victoria Police Acting Inspector Jason Benbow said. "I'm sure he's got a story to tell us soon, which we're very keen to hear," he added.

news.titleTr: Poundland set for more time to secure a rescue deal as emergency talks continue
news.summaryTr: The BBC understands the discount chain, which has been edging towards administration, will be given more time to find a buyer.
news.articleText: Poundland set for more time to secure a rescue deal as emergency talks continue - Published Poundland looks set to avoid immediate collapse after its US owners told MPs on Wednesday they were in favour of extending a deadline to find a rescue deal. The discount chain, which has 11,000 employees, has been edging towards administration after being blocked by Gordon Borthers from accessing cash in its bank accounts. A deadline to secure a buyer for the business is set to expire at midnight, but sources close to the situation told the BBC they expect more time will be given, thanks to the release funding in recent days. A committee of MPs questioned Gordon Brothers following accusations that the investment firm hopes to profit from selling off Poundland's 600 stores and stock piecemeal. Gordon Brothers - which bought the chain for just £1 last year - is accused of forcing that outcome by restricting Poundland's access to available cash needed to restock stores and pay wages and rent, ahead of the crucial Christmas trading period. The investment firm, which specialises in buying and restructuring distressed companies, has denied the claims. But pressure remains on Poundland's owners after a takeover bid was rejected. The decision prompted calls for answers from politicians, including Prime Minister Andy Burnham. About £50m had been frozen by Gordon Brothers, the BBC understands, meaning Poundland bosses were unable to restock shelves across its 600 shops. The BBC understands that Gordon Brothers agreed to release a further £9m from Poundland's accounts, on top of £10m announced earlier. This will grant the company an additional 10 days to find a new buyer. There are three bids currently on the table for Poundland, all of which have so far been rejected by the Gordon Brothers, who stand to profit from selling the company and its stock piecemeal. 'Do the right thing' Following the meeting between MPs on the business and trade committee and representatives of Gordon Brothers, chairman Liam Byrne told the BBC he was "deeply concerned" and described the firm's behaviour as "much like a wolf on Wall Street, on the British High Street". "They refused to prioritise, protecting jobs and stores over and above their own financial returns," he added. "It's clear that they've taken millions out of Poundland at a time when they themselves said the business was on a knife edge." Byrne said the committee's message to Gordon Brothers was to ensure Poundland had "access to the funds that it needs to trade at what should be one of the busiest periods in the year". He urged Gordon Brothers to "do what is right to save jobs and stores and do that now". "It's a good business, it's a much-loved business, and particularly in the middle of the cost of living crisis, communities up and down the country rely on access to the kind of stores that it operates," Byrne added. Following the private meeting with MPs, Poundland's chief executive Barry Williams told the BBC the chain's board would hold an urgent meeting on Wednesday night. Views on Poundland performance differ Views on the chain's performance differ between those running operations and the owners. Poundland boss Williams told staff last week that like-for-like sales, which exclude new store openings, were up 11.4%. The sales period included Halloween, but Williams said this was £1.5m ahead of budget. He added the business made a profit of £18.1m in the year to September, which was a "strong recovery" from the previous year where there were losses of £68m. However, Gordon Brothers has painted a different picture, saying the chain remains "challenged and vulnerable to any potential downturn in future trading". It has argued the best way of securing jobs may be to split up the business and sell chunks of its 600 sites to other retailers. There has been interest from the likes of Poundstretcher, Tesco and B&M in picking up Poundland stores which could mean continuing employment for workers in the event the chain is broken up. The main issue is whether a piecemeal sale would protect more jobs than a buyer willing to keep Poundland as a national chain. Get in touch Are you affected by issues discussed in this story? news.title: MSCI confirms Strategy’s removal from indexes at end of November
news.summary: Strategy, Metaplanet and Upexi are marked for deletion in MSCI’s final list, with changes taking effect after the Nov. 30 close.

news.titleTr: MSCI confirms Strategy’s removal from indexes at end of November
news.summaryTr: Strategy, Metaplanet and Upexi are marked for deletion in MSCI’s final list, with changes taking effect after the Nov. 30 close.
news.articleText: MSCI confirms Strategy’s removal from indexes at end of November Strategy, Metaplanet and Upexi are marked for deletion in MSCI’s final list, with changes taking effect after the Nov. 30 close. Index provider MSCI has confirmed Bitcoin treasury company Strategy will be removed from its global equity indexes, following months of debate over whether crypto treasury firms qualify as operating businesses. MSCI’s final list of affected securities, released as part of its November index review, lists “STRATEGY A” with the action “Deleted.” Japan’s Metaplanet and crypto treasury company Upexi are also marked for deletion, while Ether treasury firm Sharplink is on a watchlist. Strategy shares fell 1.65% in after-hours trading on Wednesday. The changes take effect after market close on Nov. 30, under the implementation timetable MSCI announced in October. Removal could prompt funds tracking the affected benchmarks to sell the companies’ shares, reducing a source of passive investment demand. As Cointelegraph reported in October, JPMorgan previously estimated that Strategy’s exclusion could trigger roughly $2.8 billion in selling. Strategy opposed the proposal, arguing that it repackaged MSCI’s earlier effort to exclude digital asset treasury companies and injected policy judgments into index construction. The company nevertheless played down the potential disruption. In its consultation response, Strategy said MSCI-linked funds held approximately 13 million shares, representing 3.1% of its basic shares outstanding and less than one day’s trading volume. Related: Bitcoin think tank questions MSCI’s ‘invisible committee’ over Strategy, Metaplanet rule

news.title: From Paris to DC - why offices are being turned into apartments
news.summary: Office buildings with low occupancy rates are being transformed into flats.

news.titleTr: From Paris to DC - why offices are being turned into apartments
news.summaryTr: Office buildings with low occupancy rates are being transformed into flats.
news.articleText: From Paris to DC - why offices are being turned into apartments - Published When Roland Cubin walks you round what will eventually be a new Parisian apartment you have to use your imagination. "Here you will be in the kitchen, and here is the bathroom," says the deputy CEO of French real estate company Groupama Immobilier. It all sounds appealing, an upmarket flat in the west of Paris, but presently the space doesn't look like one at all. That's because it's currently a corner of one floor of a nine-storey office building called Le Diamant, where 1,800 people work. Groupama Immobilier intends to convert the entire building into apartments. It should be the first of many such office-to-apartments conversions in the surrounding area. We are in La Défense, the purpose-built, business district of the French capital, where the city has congregated its modern skyscrapers. Mirroring a similar trend in places such as New York, Washington DC and London; Paris La Défense, the public development authority that runs the area, has unveiled plans to turn up to a fifth of the office buildings into housing. Cubin leads us into what is currently a conference room in the centre of the building. It has no windows, which is indicative of a big challenge when turning offices into apartments – what to do with the large amount of space in the middle of every floor that doesn't get any natural light. "There won't be any rooms there. Just access," says Roland Cubin, in reference to lifts and stairs. Other issues include the need for more plumbing, and ceilings that can be too low. Despite these challenges, there is a simple reason why there are plans for so many conversions – demand for offices in La Défense and across Paris has plummeted since the Covid-19 pandemic and the growth of homeworking. "La Défense has a vacancy rate of 14-15% which is higher than it used to be," says Pierre-Yves Guice, CEO of Paris La Défense. He adds that another reason for the conversion programme is the need to transform the business district from a place where the only thing people do is work. "To retain companies in France and in Western Europe we need to diversify these office landscapes of the last century, because no-one wants to work in such an environment any longer," says Guice. Ludovic Delaisse, CEO of the French arm of the Canadian real estate business Colliers, says that demand for office space in Paris has fallen by almost a third over the past five to six years. He adds that office high rises will continue to be needed, but that cities need to make sure that leisure time can be enjoyed around them, such as having restaurants, bars, cinemas and gyms on their doorstep. "People like the idea of grouping together in a centre of expertise [for work] - in tech hubs, for example. The challenge for La Défense is to be a place where you want to be, that you want to see when you leave work in the evening." Inspiration for La Défense can come from Washington DC and New York City, where tax cuts for property developers are fuelling the largest amount of office to apartment conversions in the US. Like in Paris, this is in response to falling demand for office space since the pandemic. A report last year, external found that 8,310 converted flats were in the pipeline in New York, and 6,533 in Washington. In third place was Los Angeles on 4,322, followed by Chicago on 3,606. "We set a goal of introducing 15,000 new residents downtown by 2028 and we are now on track to doing that," says Washington DC's deputy mayor for planning and development Nina Albert. She says that while "there may be one or two pretty significant building demolitions… the majority are office conversions". As in Paris, they've faced technical challenges. They've sometimes solved the natural light problem in the middle of office buildings by creating atriums – light sinks in other words – in the middle of them. Albert adds that about "hundreds of millions of dollars of private investment" has flooded into the sector. In addition to tax cuts, the DC Department of Buildings, part of the Council of the District of Columbia, has eased planning restrictions to make it easier for office conversion schemes to gain official approval in the US capital. It's a similar case in New York City. In the UK, there are also tax cuts and eased planning rules, external for converting offices into apartments. This has led to a continuing boom in conversions. A report last year by property firm Knight Frank said that the number of such projects in London were 60% higher , externalthan pre-Covid levels. Back in Paris, Cubin hopes that French authorities follow these examples and reduce both taxes and rules regarding conversions. "Just how the government deals with the tax question will decide whether France will be able to convert 2% of its vacant offices or 18 to 23%," he says. "And at the moment, when you transform a building in a way that changes its function, it is classed not as an old building that's been changed but as a new building with all the regulatory demands that go with that regarding car parking spaces, wheelchair access, fire safety and so on." - Published15 October - Published8 October

news.title: Nvidia'daki satış Asya piyasalarını da etkiledi: Nasdaq vadeli işlemleri geriledi
news.summary: Nvidia CEO'su Jensen Huang'ın görevden alınabileceği yönündeki haberlerin ardından şirket hisseleri kapanış sonrası işlemlerde yaklaşık yüzde 8 düşerken Nasdaq 100 vadeli işlemleri yüzde 1 geriledi. Asya borsalarının güne karışık başlaması bekleniyor.

news.titleTr: Nvidia'daki satış Asya piyasalarını da etkiledi: Nasdaq vadeli işlemleri geriledi
news.summaryTr: Nvidia CEO'su Jensen Huang'ın görevden alınabileceği yönündeki haberlerin ardından şirket hisseleri kapanış sonrası işlemlerde yaklaşık yüzde 8 düşerken Nasdaq 100 vadeli işlemleri yüzde 1 geriledi. Asya borsalarının güne karışık başlaması bekleniyor.
news.articleText: Nvidia'daki satış Asya piyasalarını da etkiledi: Nasdaq vadeli işlemleri geriledi - Nvidia CEO'su Jensen Huang'ın görevden alınabileceği yönündeki haberlerin ardından şirket hisseleri kapanış sonrası işlemlerde yaklaşık yüzde 8 düşerken Nasdaq 100 vadeli işlemleri yüzde 1 geriledi. Asya borsalarının güne karışık başlaması bekleniyor. ABD vadeli endeksleri, Nvidia hisselerinde yeniden başlayan satışların etkisiyle çarşamba akşamı geriledi. Teknoloji ağırlıklı Nasdaq 100 vadeli işlemleri yüzde 1 düşerken S&P 500 vadeli işlemleri yüzde 0,4 değer kaybetti. Dow Jones vadeli işlemleri ise yatay seyretti. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Nvidia hisseleri, şirketin yönetim kurulunun CEO Jensen Huang'ı görevden almayı değerlendirdiğine ilişkin Wall Street Journal (WSJ) haberinin ardından kapanış sonrası işlemlerde yaklaşık yüzde 8 geriledi. New York Times da gün içinde Huang'ın şirket yöneticilerinden biriyle evlilik dışı ilişki yaşadığını öne sürmüştü. ABD borsaları günü yükselişle tamamladı Vadeli işlemlerdeki düşüşe karşın ABD borsaları normal işlem gününü yükselişle tamamladı. Dow Jones Sanayi Endeksi yaklaşık 255 puan, yüzde 0,5 yükseldi. S&P 500 yüzde 1,3, Nasdaq Bileşik Endeksi ise yüzde 1,6 değer kazandı. Yükselişte, bilançosunun ardından hisseleri değer kazanan CoreWeave ve Nvidia'daki toparlanma etkili oldu. Yatırımcılar, Nvidia'daki son dalgalanmaya rağmen yapay zeka odaklı yükselişin devam edip edemeyeceğini değerlendiriyor. CoreWeave'in beklentileri aşan sonuçları ve gelir tahminini yükseltmesi ise yapay zeka yatırımlarının uzun vadeli büyüme potansiyeline ilişkin iyimserliği destekledi. Piyasalarda yapay zeka iyimserliği ve enflasyon endişesi karşı karşıya Wells Fargo Investment Institute Küresel Hisse Senetleri ve Reel Varlıklar Başkanı Sameer Samana, yapay zeka iyimserliğine rağmen yatırımcıların temkinli hareket etmesi gerektiğini söyledi. Samana; enflasyonun dirençli seyretmesi, Fed'in faiz artırımlarına devam etme ihtimali, uzun vadeli faizlerin yükselmesi ve Washington'daki politika değişikliklerinin yanı sıra yapay zeka ve veri merkezlerine yönelik düzenleme taleplerinin piyasalarda risk oluşturduğunu belirtti. Plancorp Yatırım Stratejisi Direktörü Callie Cox da yapay zeka beklentileri ile faiz ve enflasyon endişeleri arasındaki gerilimin piyasa algısını baskılayabileceğini ifade etti. Gözler ABD istihdam ve konut verilerinde Yatırımcılar, enflasyonun, iş gücü piyasasının ve genel ekonomik görünümün seyrine ilişkin yeni ipuçları için ekonomik verileri takip ediyor. Perşembe günü ABD'de saat 08.30'da haftalık işsizlik maaşı başvuruları, saat 10.00'da ise ikinci el konut satışları verileri açıklanacak. Asya borsalarında karışık açılış bekleniyor Nvidia hisselerindeki düşüşün ardından Asya-Pasifik piyasalarının perşembe gününe karışık başlaması bekleniyor. Japonya'nın Nikkei 225 endeksine ilişkin vadeli işlemler Chicago'da 61.760, Osaka'da ise 62.020 seviyesinde işlem gördü. Nikkei 225'in önceki kapanışı 61.248,59 seviyesindeydi. Hong Kong Hang Seng endeksi vadeli işlemleri 24.107 puanda bulunurken endeksin önceki kapanışı 24.315,92 olmuştu. Avustralya S&P/ASX 200 endeksi ise erken işlemlerde yüzde 0,31 geriledi.

ABD borsaları günü yükselişle tamamladı Vadeli işlemlerdeki düşüşe karşın ABD borsaları normal işlem gününü yükselişle tamamladı. Dow Jones Sanayi Endeksi yaklaşık 255 puan, yüzde 0,5 yükseldi. S&P 500 yüzde 1,3, Nasdaq Bileşik Endeksi ise yüzde 1,6 değer kazandı. Yükselişte, bilançosunun ardından hisseleri değer kazanan CoreWeave ve Nvidia'daki toparlanma etkili oldu. Yatırımcılar, Nvidia'daki son dalgalanmaya rağmen yapay zeka odaklı yükselişin devam edip edemeyeceğini değerlendiriyor. CoreWeave'in beklentileri aşan sonuçları ve gelir tahminini yükseltmesi ise yapay zeka yatırımlarının uzun vadeli büyüme potansiyeline ilişkin iyimserliği destekledi. Piyasalarda yapay zeka iyimserliği ve enflasyon endişesi karşı karşıya Wells Fargo Investment Institute Küresel Hisse Senetleri ve Reel Varlıklar Başkanı Sameer Samana, yapay zeka iyimserliğine rağmen yatırımcıların temkinli hareket etmesi gerektiğini söyledi. Samana; enflasyonun dirençli seyretmesi, Fed'in faiz artırımlarına devam etme ihtimali, uzun vadeli faizlerin yükselmesi ve Washington'daki politika değişikliklerinin yanı sıra yapay zeka ve veri merkezlerine yönelik düzenleme taleplerinin piyasalarda risk oluşturduğunu belirtti. Plancorp Yatırım Stratejisi Direktörü Callie Cox da yapay zeka beklentileri ile faiz ve enflasyon endişeleri arasındaki gerilimin piyasa algısını baskılayabileceğini ifade etti. Gözler ABD istihdam ve konut verilerinde Yatırımcılar, enflasyonun, iş gücü piyasasının ve genel ekonomik görünümün seyrine ilişkin yeni ipuçları için ekonomik verileri takip ediyor. Perşembe günü ABD'de saat 08.30'da haftalık işsizlik maaşı başvuruları, saat 10.00'da ise ikinci el konut satışları verileri açıklanacak. Asya borsalarında karışık açılış bekleniyor Nvidia hisselerindeki düşüşün ardından Asya-Pasifik piyasalarının perşembe gününe karışık başlaması bekleniyor. Japonya'nın Nikkei 225 endeksine ilişkin vadeli işlemler Chicago'da 61.760, Osaka'da ise 62.020 seviyesinde işlem gördü. Nikkei 225'in önceki kapanışı 61.248,59 seviyesindeydi. Hong Kong Hang Seng endeksi vadeli işlemleri 24.107 puanda bulunurken endeksin önceki kapanışı 24.315,92 olmuştu. Avustralya S&P/ASX 200 endeksi ise erken işlemlerde yüzde 0,31 geriledi.

news.title: Some under-25s should get fewer benefits, Milburn review to say
news.summary: The proposed radical overhaul of the welfare system would move under-25s off the main sickness benefits.

news.titleTr: Some under-25s should get fewer benefits, Milburn review to say
news.summaryTr: The proposed radical overhaul of the welfare system would move under-25s off the main sickness benefits.
news.articleText: Some under-25s should get fewer benefits, Milburn review to say - Published Some young people could see reductions to the benefits they are entitled to, under a radical overhaul of the system to be recommended by a government-commissioned review. Alan Milburn's year-long report, which will be published on Tuesday, will recommend moving under-25s off the main sickness and disability benefits, the Times reported, external. Milburn, a former Labour health secretary, has been tasked by the government with helping reduce the one in eight 18- to 24-year-olds in the UK who are not in education, employment or training - or "Neet". He said on Wednesday night that his plans would not be "pain-free" and would affect both existing and new claimants. His report is expected to recommend that under-25s are no longer able to claim the health element of universal credit or personal independence payment (Pip). Instead, they would receive an allowance on the same basic rate as universal credit. Some could be eligible for a new "additional cost allowance" to cover day-to-day costs related to their conditions. But many claimants would receive less under the plans, which the government is set to take forward into legislation in the new year. Milburn, a Labour MP from 1992 to 2010, is also expected to recommend an investment of billions into more employment support for young people, including work placements, job subsidies and one-to-one personal advisers. Those with more severe disabilities and unable to work would get a new benefit paid at a higher rate. Speaking to the Times about his report, Milburn said: "Candidly, it could mean that some people will get less financial support at the beginning of their benefit claim than under the current system. "But actually, for young people, there's a different debate that we've got to resolve, which is whether the priority is their longer-term life chances or just their immediate shorter-term finances. "I think what the current system does [is] it prioritises the latter over the former. I believe that's the wrong choice and it needs to be the other way around." Just under one million young people in the UK are Neets, data from the Office for National Statistics (ONS) from April to June suggests. This was a rise of 3% on the same period last year. Milburn's recommendations are likely to be backed by Prime Minister Andy Burnham but could prove controversial among Labour MPs, who opposed welfare reform under his predecessor Sir Keir Starmer. The reforms would represent a radical overhaul of Britain's welfare system, at a time when there is heavy political pressure for the UK to find the money to spend more on defence. If Milburn's recommendations were approved, it could take almost a decade for the British state to see monetary savings. The new system "will need significant investment" and would involve "rebuilding the system from scratch," Milburn added. He said that currently "you've got hundreds of thousands of young people stuck in a benefit system that is trapping them in poverty, giving them no prospect of prosperity or a job". His new proposed system would involve an element of carrot and stick, where young people could lose some of their benefits if they did not engage with the extra work support options. "A deal isn't a deal unless there are potential consequences," Milburn said. "Entitlements and responsibilities are two sides of the same coin." A government spokesperson said: "We will always ensure there is a safety net for the most vulnerable and those who are unable to work. "But the prime minister has been clear that we need a wholesale change in the way we support young people to grow up in this country, where we invest in their success rather than paying for failure." news.title: Suiet wallet to shut down in latest exit from Sui ecosystem
news.summary: The self-custodial wallet will keep its API services running through Nov. 14. Sui’s DeFi total value locked has fallen more than 22% over the past month.

news.titleTr: Suiet wallet to shut down in latest exit from Sui ecosystem
news.summaryTr: The self-custodial wallet will keep its API services running through Nov. 14. Sui’s DeFi total value locked has fallen more than 22% over the past month.
news.articleText: Suiet wallet to shut down in latest exit from Sui ecosystem The self-custodial wallet will keep its API services running through Nov. 14. Sui’s DeFi total value locked has fallen more than 22% over the past month. Cryptocurrency wallet Suiet is shutting down, adding to a series of closures and service withdrawals in the Sui ecosystem. Suiet, a self-custodial wallet built for the Sui blockchain, said in a notice that it will stop updating and supporting its wallet, with API services set to end after Nov. 14. The shutdown comes as the Sui network has seen a sharp decline in decentralized finance (DeFi) activity. Sui’s total value locked (TVL) stood at about $413 million on Wednesday, down more than 22% over the past month, according to DefiLlama data. Data from Token Terminal shows that Sui averaged about 128,000 daily active users in October, down from 601,000 in November 2025 – or around a 79% drop. Meanwhile, other recent closures have also raised concerns about the costs and challenges of keeping projects running on the Sui network. “Sui’s problems seem to mostly be of an economic nature resulting from expensive engineering costs and low user volume rather than protocol failures,” Kadan Stadelmann, former chief technology officer of Komodo Platform, told Cointelegraph. “No flaw in the system’s core design has been found.” Cointelegraph reached out to the Sui Foundation and Suiet for comment but had not received responses by publication. Related: Sui DeFi protocol Full Sail to wind down after Switchboard incident Recent closures and departures Suiet’s shutdown immediately follows the Sui-based hardware wallet project Suiball also announcing its closure on Nov. 10. Meanwhile wallet provider Phantom ended support for Sui in September. DeFi project Full Sail also shut down following a security incident involving Switchboard that caused about $91,000 in losses. Despite the decline in active users, transactions on Sui have increased, reaching 324 million in October, up from 101 million in November 2025, according to Token Terminal. However, more transactions do not necessarily mean more users, and wallet providers must still decide whether supporting the network is worth the cost, according to Stadelmann. “Multi-chain wallets have expansive attack surfaces, and Sui’s approach adds costs for vendors who can take their business to less capital intensive chains,” he said. “Any individual failure of a multi-chain wallet is more a reflection of the risks rather than an indictment of any given protocol.” A series of outages Sui has also experienced four network outages in 2026, resulting in around 22 hours of combined downtime, according to reports published by the Sui Foundation. The network stopped processing transactions for about six hours in January, followed by three more outages on May 28 and 29. The May disruptions were linked to software bugs, including problems introduced by a network update, the Sui Foundation said at the time. By comparison, rival blockchain Solana has not recorded a network-wide outage since February 2024, when it went offline for nearly five hours. Meanwhile, Aptos, which uses the same underlying smart contract programming language as Sui, last reported a mainnet outage in October 2023. Network outages are significant because they can prevent DeFi users from trading, transferring funds or managing positions, although the Sui Foundation said no user funds were at risk during its May disruptions. news.title: Nvidia preparing to oust CEO Jensen Huang after affairs: WSJ
news.summary: The report about Huang’s possible departure came after the New York Times reported that he had a second extramarital affair.

news.titleTr: Nvidia preparing to oust CEO Jensen Huang after affairs: WSJ
news.summaryTr: The report about Huang’s possible departure came after the New York Times reported that he had a second extramarital affair.
news.articleText: Nvidia preparing to oust CEO Jensen Huang after affairs: WSJ The report about Huang’s possible departure came after the New York Times reported that he had a second extramarital affair. Nvidia’s board is preparing to oust founder and CEO Jensen Huang after he had two extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy, The Wall Street Journal reported. Directors could meet as soon as Wednesday to determine Huang’s future, the report said, citing people familiar with the matter. His potential removal would mark a major leadership change for the chipmaker, which has become central to the artificial intelligence boom under Huang. Cointelegraph reached out to Nvidia for comment but did not receive an immediate response. One affair involved Alice Huang, an executive at Singapore-based data company Megaspeed, a major Nvidia customer. US intelligence officials believe she was a spy for Beijing. The New York Times reported Wednesday that Huang also had an extramarital affair with Nvidia’s vice president of health care, Kimberly Powell, according to five people who worked at the company. On Sunday, Huang acknowledged being unfaithful to his wife in a letter to employees, apologizing for breaching their trust. “I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did,” he wrote. Huang also confirmed that Nvidia’s board had launched an independent investigation into national security concerns raised in news reports. He pledged to cooperate fully and said he remained committed to the company. Nvidia shares fell 8% to $159.76 in after-hours trading following the reports, reversing a 2.9% gain during the regular session, according to Google Finance data. news.summaryTr: Wall Street Journal, Nvidia yönetim kurulunun iki ayrı ilişki iddiası ve Çin istihbaratıyla bağlantılı olduğu öne sürülen bir kadınla ilişkisi nedeniyle CEO Jensen Huang'ın görevden alınmasını değerlendirdiğini yazdı. Nvidia hisseleri kapanış sonrası işlemlerde yüzde 8 geriledi.
news.articleText: Nvidia'da deprem! WSJ: Yönetim kurulu Jensen Huang'ı görevden almayı değerlendiriyor - Wall Street Journal, Nvidia yönetim kurulunun iki ayrı ilişki iddiası ve Çin istihbaratıyla bağlantılı olduğu öne sürülen bir kadınla ilişkisi nedeniyle CEO Jensen Huang'ın görevden alınmasını değerlendirdiğini yazdı. Nvidia hisseleri kapanış sonrası işlemlerde yüzde 8 geriledi. Nvidia yönetim kurulunun, CEO Jensen Huang'ın iki ayrı evlilik dışı ilişki yaşadığına yönelik haberlerin ardından görevden alınması seçeneğini değerlendirdiği öne sürüldü. Wall Street Journal'ın (WSJ) konuya yakın kaynaklara dayandırdığı haberine göre yönetim kurulu, Huang'ın geleceğini görüşmek üzere 11 Kasım Çarşamba günü toplanmaya hazırlanıyor. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Reuters'ın aktardığı WSJ haberinde, söz konusu ilişkilerden birinin Çinli casus olduğundan şüphelenilen bir kadınla yaşandığı iddia edildi. Yönetim kurulunun Huang'ın görevine devam edip etmeyeceğine ilişkin karar vermek üzere bir araya gelmesinin beklendiği belirtildi. Nvidia'dan henüz açıklama gelmedi Nvidia, Reuters'ın konuya ilişkin yorum talebine hemen yanıt vermedi. Gün içinde New York Times da Huang'ın doğrudan kendisine bağlı çalışan bir şirket yöneticisiyle evlilik dışı ilişki yaşadığını öne sürmüştü. Böylece Nvidia CEO'su hakkında aynı gün içinde iki ayrı ilişki iddiası gündeme geldi. Yönetim kurulu yabancı istihbarat iddiasını araştırıyor Gelişmeler, Huang'ın eşine sadık kalmadığını kabul etmesinden ve Nvidia yönetim kurulunun, CEO'nun yabancı bir istihbarat operasyonunun hedefi olup olmadığını araştırmaya başlamasından günler sonra yaşandı. Şirket yönetiminin yürüttüğü incelemenin, Çin istihbaratıyla bağlantılı olduğu şüphesi bulunan bir kadınla ilişki iddiasını da kapsadığı bildirildi. Nvidia hisselerinde sert düşüş Huang hakkındaki haberlerin ardından Nvidia hisseleri borsa kapanışı sonrasındaki işlemlerde yaklaşık yüzde 8 değer kaybetti. Şirket yönetim kurulunun Huang'ın geleceğine ilişkin nasıl bir karar alacağı ise belirsizliğini koruyor.

news.summaryTr: Acıbadem Üniversitesi 25, Doğuş Üniversitesi 15 olmak üzere iki üniversite toplam 40 akademik personel alacak. Profesör, doçent, doktor öğretim üyesi ve araştırma görevlisi kadroları için başvuru ve sınav takvimi açıklandı.
news.articleText: İki üniversiteden 40 akademik personel alımı! Başvurular başladı - Acıbadem Üniversitesi 25, Doğuş Üniversitesi 15 olmak üzere iki üniversite toplam 40 akademik personel alacak. Profesör, doçent, doktor öğretim üyesi ve araştırma görevlisi kadroları için başvuru ve sınav takvimi açıklandı. İstanbul'daki Acıbadem Mehmet Ali Aydınlar Üniversitesi ve Doğuş Üniversitesi, toplam 40 akademik personel istihdam etmek üzere ilana çıktı. Profesör, doçent, doktor öğretim üyesi, öğretim görevlisi ve araştırma görevlisi kadrolarını kapsayan alımlarda son başvuru tarihleri ve aranan şartlar açıklandı. Acıbadem Üniversitesi 25 akademisyen alacak CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Acıbadem Mehmet Ali Aydınlar Üniversitesi, 18 öğretim üyesi ile 7 öğretim görevlisi ve araştırma görevlisi olmak üzere toplam 25 kişilik kadro açtı. Üniversitenin öğretim üyesi alımları kapsamında 7 profesör, 3 doçent ve 8 doktor öğretim üyesi istihdam edilecek. Kadroların bulunduğu alanlar arasında şunlar yer alıyor: - Genel cerrahi - Ortopedi ve travmatoloji - Kulak burun boğaz - Kardiyoloji - Moleküler biyoloji ve genetik - Bilgisayar mühendisliği - Beslenme ve diyetetik - Gastronomi Üniversite ayrıca radyasyon onkolojisi ve patoloji laboratuvar teknikleri alanlarında öğretim görevlisi; eczacılık, hemşirelik, beslenme ve diyetetik ile medikal biyoteknoloji alanlarında araştırma görevlisi alacak. Öğretim üyeliği kadrolarına başvuruların ilan tarihinden itibaren 15 gün içinde şahsen yapılması gerekiyor. Öğretim görevlisi ve araştırma görevlisi kadroları için son başvuru tarihi 26 Kasım 2026 olarak açıklandı. Bu kadrolara başvuracak adayların ALES'ten en az 70 puan alması gerekiyor. Yabancı dille eğitim veren bölümlerde ise yabancı dil puanına ilişkin ek koşullar aranacak. Doğuş Üniversitesi 15 kişilik kadro açtı Doğuş Üniversitesi, 9 öğretim üyesi ve 6 öğretim görevlisi olmak üzere toplam 15 akademik personel istihdam edecek. Öğretim üyesi alımları şu alanlarda gerçekleştirilecek: - Hukuk - Psikoloji - Uluslararası ticaret ve işletmecilik - Siyaset bilimi ve kamu yönetimi - Görsel iletişim tasarımı - Hemşirelik - Yazılım geliştirme - Endüstri mühendisliği Üniversitenin meslek yüksekokulunda ise mekatronik, dijital dönüşüm elektroniği, robotik ve yapay zekâ, imalat yürütme sistemleri operatörlüğü ile internet ve ağ teknolojileri programlarına öğretim görevlisi alınacak. Öğretim görevlisi kadrolarına başvuracak adayların ALES'ten en az 70 puan almış ve ilgili alanlarda en az tezli yüksek lisans derecesine sahip olması gerekiyor. Başvuru tarihleri ve sınav takvimi açıklandı Doğuş Üniversitesi'nin akademik personel alımı için başvurular 12 Kasım'da başladı. Son başvuru tarihi 26 Kasım 2026 saat 17.00 olarak belirlendi. Doğuş Üniversitesi'nin sınav takvimi şöyle: - 30 Kasım: Ön değerlendirme sonuçları - 1 Aralık: Giriş sınavı - 3 Aralık: Nihai sonuçların açıklanması Acıbadem Üniversitesi'nin öğretim görevlisi ve araştırma görevlisi kadroları için takvim ise şöyle: - 30 Kasım: Ön değerlendirme sonuçları - 2 Aralık: Giriş sınavı - 4 Aralık: Nihai sonuçların açıklanması Başvurular, üniversitelerin ilanlarında belirtilen ilgili birimlere şahsen veya izin verilen kadrolarda posta yoluyla yapılabilecek. İnternet üzerinden başvuru kabul edilmeyecek. İzmir Kâtip Çelebi Üniversitesi'nin ilanında değişiklik Öte yandan İzmir Kâtip Çelebi Üniversitesi de 2 Kasım 2026 tarihli öğretim üyesi alım ilanında değişikliğe gitti. Üniversite, İktisadi ve İdari Bilimler Fakültesi Sağlık Yönetimi Bölümü Hastane İşletmeciliği Ana Bilim Dalı için açılan 7 numaralı profesör kadrosunun şartlarını güncelledi. Aynı ilanda bulunan 18 numaralı öğretim üyesi kadrosu ise iptal edildi.

news.title: Zelenskiy'den üçlü zirve mesajı: Putin, Trump ve Kiev aynı masaya gelebilir
news.summary: Zelenskiy, Rusya-Ukrayna Savaşı'nı sona erdirmek için Trump, Putin ve kendisinin katılacağı üçlü zirveye yönelik görüşmelerin sürdüğünü açıkladı. Abu Dabi'deki müzakerelerde 1.200 esire kadar takas ve güvenlik garantileri de gündeme geldi.

news.titleTr: Zelenskiy'den üçlü zirve mesajı: Putin, Trump ve Kiev aynı masaya gelebilir
news.summaryTr: Zelenskiy, Rusya-Ukrayna Savaşı'nı sona erdirmek için Trump, Putin ve kendisinin katılacağı üçlü zirveye yönelik görüşmelerin sürdüğünü açıkladı. Abu Dabi'deki müzakerelerde 1.200 esire kadar takas ve güvenlik garantileri de gündeme geldi.
news.articleText: Zelenskiy'den üçlü zirve mesajı: Putin, Trump ve Kiev aynı masaya gelebilir - Zelenskiy, Rusya-Ukrayna Savaşı'nı sona erdirmek için Trump, Putin ve kendisinin katılacağı üçlü zirveye yönelik görüşmelerin sürdüğünü açıkladı. Abu Dabi'deki müzakerelerde 1.200 esire kadar takas ve güvenlik garantileri de gündeme geldi. Ukrayna Devlet Başkanı Volodimir Zelenskiy, Rusya ile savaşı sona erdirmek amacıyla ABD, Rusya ve Ukrayna liderlerini bir araya getirecek üçlü zirve için görüşmelerin sürdüğünü açıkladı. Abu Dabi'deki müzakerelerde esir takası, güvenlik garantileri ve enerji altyapılarına yönelik saldırıların durdurulması da gündeme geldi. Abu Dabi'de 1.200 esirin takası gündemde CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle İrlanda'nın başkenti Dublin'de Başbakan Micheal Martin ile bir araya gelen Zelenskiy, ortak basın toplantısında Rusya-Ukrayna Savaşı'na ilişkin diplomatik temasları değerlendirdi. Zelenskiy, 10-11 Kasım'da Birleşik Arap Emirlikleri'nin başkenti Abu Dabi'de ABD, Rusya ve Ukrayna heyetlerinin katılımıyla üçlü müzakereler gerçekleştirildiğini hatırlattı. Görüşmelerde tarafların biner esiri takas etmesi seçeneğinin ele alındığını belirten Zelenskiy, takasın 1.200 esire çıkarılmasının da mümkün olabileceğini söyledi. Ukrayna lideri, müzakerelerde ülkesine yönelik farklı güvenlik garantisi modellerinin de değerlendirildiğini ifade etti. Kiev'den enerji saldırıları ve denizde ateşkes önerisi Zelenskiy, Ukrayna'nın müzakerelerde Rusya'ya enerji altyapılarına yönelik saldırıların durdurulmasını ve denizde ateşkes sağlanmasını önerdiğini açıkladı. Ancak Rus heyetinin bu konularda karar verme yetkisi bulunmadığını savunan Zelenskiy, görüşmelerde henüz somut bir sonuca ulaşılamadığını belirtti. Putin ile görüşmede üçlü zirve gündeme gelecek Abu Dabi'deki görüşmelere katılan ABD'li yetkililerin 12 Kasım'da Rusya Devlet Başkanı Vladimir Putin ile bir araya gelmesi bekleniyor. Zelenskiy, ABD Başkanı Donald Trump'ın damadı ve Özel Temsilcisi Jared Kushner ile Trump'ın Özel Temsilcisi Steve Witkoff'un Putin'le yapacağı görüşmede üçlü zirve konusunu gündeme getirmesini beklediklerini söyledi. Ukrayna lideri, ABD, Rusya ve Ukrayna liderlerinin bir araya gelmesinin savaşın sona erdirilmesine ilişkin kritik başlıkların ele alınması açısından önemli olduğunu vurguladı. Üçlü zirvenin gerçekleştirilmesi ihtimalinin ve liderler düzeyinde görüşme için tarafların atması gereken adımların müzakere edildiğini belirten Zelenskiy, sürecin büyük ölçüde ABD ile Rusya arasındaki temaslara bağlı olduğunu ifade etti. Zelenskiy: Avrupa da müzakere masasında olmalı Ukrayna Devlet Başkanı, Avrupa ülkelerinin de barış görüşmelerinde yer alması gerektiğini söyledi. Zelenskiy, ABD tarafının Avrupa'nın sürece katılımına daha olumlu yaklaştığını belirtti. Zelenskiy ayrıca Dublin'deki temasları kapsamında Kushner ve Witkoff ile de görüşebileceğini açıkladı.

news.summary: Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.

news.titleTr: Here’s what happened in crypto today
news.summaryTr: Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.
news.articleText: Here’s what happened in crypto today Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation. Today in crypto, OKX and Intercontinental Exchange are preparing to launch tokenized stock trading on Nov. 23 despite objections from major companies, Barclays increased its holdings in BlackRock’s Bitcoin ETF by 48% in the third quarter, and pro-crypto lawmaker Tom Emmer was elected House Republican minority whip as Democrats prepare to take control of Congress. OKXICE moves ahead with tokenized stocks as blue chips push back Crypto exchange OKX and New York Stock Exchange parent Intercontinental Exchange (ICE) are set to launch tokenized stock trading on Nov. 23, despite objections from 67 companies to having their shares listed and warnings from Nasdaq that trading across disconnected platforms could fragment liquidity. The venture, known as OKXICE, will operate under the US Securities and Exchange Commission’s temporary Innovation Exemption and offer eligible US customers round-the-clock trading. Under the exemption, venues must give companies a chance to object before listing shares tokenized by an unaffiliated third party. JPMorgan Chase, McDonald’s, SpaceX and Coca-Cola were among the companies that objected. Tokenized stocks are blockchain-based tokens that represent company shares or track their price. The rights they carry depend on how they are structured. The distributed value of tokenized stocks and ETFs reached $3.88 billion on Nov. 11, up 13.4% over 30 days. In comments to Cointelegraph, former New York governor and OKXICE co-chair Andrew Cuomo said investors would have “the same rights, protections and ownership that come with the underlying shares.” Barclays boosts BlackRock Bitcoin ETF stake 48% as banks expand holdings Barclays reported holding 3.94 million shares in BlackRock’s spot Bitcoin exchange-traded fund (ETF) at the end of the third quarter, up 48% from the previous quarter. The position in the iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF (IBIT) was worth about $187 million on Sept. 30, up from $88.5 million for 2.66 million shares on June 30, according to Barclays’ Friday Form 13F filing. “Early readings suggest longer-term holders make up a growing share of the spot bitcoin ETF investor base,” Bitwise analyst Camran Khosravi told Cointelegraph, pointing to increased bank exposure, including at Citigroup. Citigroup reported a new position worth about $119 million in the Fidelity Wise Origin Bitcoin Fund (FBTC). Its reported IBIT holdings also rose 50% to about 521,000 shares, from 347,000 at the end of June. The filings offer an early indication of changing institutional Bitcoin ETF ownership, with more major banks and hedge funds yet to disclose their third-quarter positions. Institutional investment managers have until Monday to file their third-quarter holdings reports. Crypto ally Tom Emmer elected House GOP minority whip Pro-crypto US Representative Tom Emmer has been elected House Republican minority whip, securing the party’s second-highest leadership position as Democrats prepare to take control of Congress in January. Emmer beat Texas Representative August Pfluger in a 103-76 secret ballot vote, according to Politico. He previously served as House Republican majority whip and will remain the party’s No. 2 leader, this time under incoming Minority Leader Jim Jordan. As minority whip, Emmer will be responsible for rallying Republican votes, coordinating the party’s legislative strategy and helping maintain unity on key bills. “Tom has been one of the strongest advocates for digital assets in Congress, and he has led the fight against a government-controlled CBDC and stood up for American innovators,” GOP Senator Cynthia Lummis said on X.

In comments to Cointelegraph, former New York governor and OKXICE co-chair Andrew Cuomo said investors would have “the same rights, protections and ownership that come with the underlying shares.” Barclays boosts BlackRock Bitcoin ETF stake 48% as banks expand holdings Barclays reported holding 3.94 million shares in BlackRock’s spot Bitcoin exchange-traded fund (ETF) at the end of the third quarter, up 48% from the previous quarter. The position in the iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF (IBIT) was worth about $187 million on Sept. 30, up from $88.5 million for 2.66 million shares on June 30, according to Barclays’ Friday Form 13F filing. “Early readings suggest longer-term holders make up a growing share of the spot bitcoin ETF investor base,” Bitwise analyst Camran Khosravi told Cointelegraph, pointing to increased bank exposure, including at Citigroup. Citigroup reported a new position worth about $119 million in the Fidelity Wise Origin Bitcoin Fund (FBTC). Its reported IBIT holdings also rose 50% to about 521,000 shares, from 347,000 at the end of June. The filings offer an early indication of changing institutional Bitcoin ETF ownership, with more major banks and hedge funds yet to disclose their third-quarter positions. Institutional investment managers have until Monday to file their third-quarter holdings reports. Crypto ally Tom Emmer elected House GOP minority whip Pro-crypto US Representative Tom Emmer has been elected House Republican minority whip, securing the party’s second-highest leadership position as Democrats prepare to take control of Congress in January. Emmer beat Texas Representative August Pfluger in a 103-76 secret ballot vote, according to Politico. He previously served as House Republican majority whip and will remain the party’s No. 2 leader, this time under incoming Minority Leader Jim Jordan. As minority whip, Emmer will be responsible for rallying Republican votes, coordinating the party’s legislative strategy and helping maintain unity on key bills. “Tom has been one of the strongest advocates for digital assets in Congress, and he has led the fight against a government-controlled CBDC and stood up for American innovators,” GOP Senator Cynthia Lummis said on X.

news.titleTr: Clashes erupt in Barcelona after thousands join Spain general strike
news.summaryTr: Tens of thousands of people have been taking part in the strike, called by the country's main unions over housing and the high cost of living.
news.articleText: Clashes erupt in Barcelona after thousands join Spain general strike - Published Clashes have broken out between groups of masked men and police in Barcelona after tens of thousands of people took part in Spain's first general strike for 14 years, called by the country's main unions over housing and the high cost of living. Some 120,000 people joined a demonstration in the capital Madrid and more than 50,000 turned out in Barcelona, where footage showed masked men setting fire to rubbish bins and smashing shop windows as police fired tear gas. Transport and other public services across Spain faced serious disruption. Spaniards are due to vote in parliamentary elections on 29 November. The head of the big UGT labour union, Pepe Álvarez, said the strike was a success with "massive" participation, while Unai Sordo of the CC OO union said turnout was "very significant." There was a heavy police presence in the centre of Barcelona on Wednesday evening, with officers wearing helmets and riot shields. Some of the disturbances took place in the Passeig de Gràcia, close to the iconic Plaça de Catalunya in the centre of the city. Small fires burned in the middle of the streets as bins were set alight. Local media reported that a group of people fired fireworks towards police and looted shops including the Lego store. Protesters were also seen trying to enter the Apple Store. The BBC spoke to a woman who attended the protests in Barcelona who said it was mostly very peaceful and "joyful". She said she was there to protest about the housing costs and that "there were a lot of children and old people there." She was in the area of Las Ramblas in the evening and saw fires in the streets. "The fires were everywhere, it was very intense," she said. Earlier in the day there was major disruption around Madrid and Barcelona, with traffic halted on several main roads. The interior ministry said dozens of people were arrested for a variety of incidents and Spanish reports said estate agencies had seen attacks on their offices. "We've completely brought the city to a standstill," a protester in Madrid told Reuters news agency, adding there was widespread support for the general strike. "Everyone's out there, despite the rainy weather; everyone's out on the streets." Another protester, 37-year-old teacher Olga Domingo, said she was protesting because "the housing situation is outrageous. The current cost of living compared to wages is completely unsustainable". The strike was triggered by widespread protests over affordable housing and rising living costs, after the eviction of 87-year-old Maricarmen Abascal from a flat in Madrid where she had lived for seven decades. She died in hospital weeks later. Rental prices in the capital have risen in recent years. The monthly cost of a 50 sq m apartment in Madrid was an average of €1,170 ($1,300; £1,000) in October, according to property portal Idealista, while Spain's average gross monthly salary is about €2,460. That amounts to nearly half the average gross salary, well above the 30% level of affordability often recommended by housing experts and public institutions. Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez called snap elections last month after parliament failed to approve his plan for housing reform. Not since 2012, under the conservative government of Mariano Rajoy, has Spain held general strikes. And while previous strikes have been problematic for the government in power, this one is different. Sánchez and his ministers have even encouraged workers to down tools and demand affordable housing. "Your eight-hour day. Your pension. Your public healthcare… These were collective conquests," he wrote on social media, praising those who took part in previous strikes. The conservative People's Party (PP), by contrast, has accused the government of attempting to weaponise the strike for electoral gain. PP leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo called the general strike "nonsense", calling the unions "mafia" and "trash". Feijoo's party is leading in the polls and party spokesman Miguel Tellado accused the government of exploiting the strike to warn voters against allowing a right-wing government to be formed, which looks the most likely outcome of the 29 November election. Sánchez told Spanish TV this week: "What is nonsense is to question the rights of workers to strike." Among those taking part in the general strike was Gonzalo Álvarez, 27, who was visiting different picket lines in central Madrid. Although he works in sales, he has been volunteering for a housing union that tries to protect tenants and makes them aware of their rights. The eviction of Maricarmen Abascal at the end of September "was the little fire" that sparked this protest, he told the BBC. Álvarez knew the 87-year-old, who had faced a tripling of her rent under new landlords, and says he was deeply upset by her treatment. He rents a small, one-bedroom flat with his girlfriend, a dental hygienist, in the city's southern Arganzuela disrict. The couple pay €1,000 between them, which means each spends about half of their salary on housing, even before other bills. "It's absolutely crazy… with the food, with the electricity, with the water, with gas." He sees no way of getting on the property ladder: "You have to collect an insane amount of money to be able to buy a house. So with these salaries, it's impossible." With current rent and purchase prices, he believes buying somewhere is "completely impossible". However, the vice-president of the CEOE, Spanish biggest business association, Miguel Garrido, criticised the strike, complaining that businesses had little to do with the price of housing. "This is not a strike for labour-related reasons, but rather for political ones, and it is closely linked to the early calling of elections," he said. Demonstrations were planned for some of Spain's biggest cities later in the day and the scale of support will be widely viewed as an indicator of public discontent ahead of the election. Another reliable indicator of support for strikes is the level of demand for electricity with Spain's industrial sector. Power usage in Spain fell by 7.5% during the early hours of Wednesday, according to data from operator Red Eléctrica. During the last general strike 14 years ago, equivalent consumption was down by more than 15%. news.title: Uncalled US House races could send more crypto allies to Congress
news.summary: The remaining races feature pro-crypto candidates and others without a stated position, giving advocacy groups what they see as “an opportunity” for outreach.

news.titleTr: Uncalled US House races could send more crypto allies to Congress
news.summaryTr: The remaining races feature pro-crypto candidates and others without a stated position, giving advocacy groups what they see as “an opportunity” for outreach.
news.articleText: Uncalled US House races could send more crypto allies to Congress The remaining races feature pro-crypto candidates and others without a stated position, giving advocacy groups what they see as “an opportunity” for outreach. Just over a week after a “blue wave” handed Democrats control of the US House and Senate, 14 races have yet to be called. The results so far have added crypto supporters in both chambers and the remaining races could bring more into Congress. Three candidates in the uncalled races received backing from crypto political action committees (PACs). According to Stand With Crypto, every candidate in those races is either strongly pro-crypto or has no stated position. As crypto advocacy groups look ahead to 2028, they’re turning their attention to candidates who have yet to take a public stance on crypto. House races still to be called Crypto PACs backed three candidates in US House races that remain undecided. Two incumbents lead in Alaska and North Carolina, while a Louisiana state senator faces a December runoff. Rep. Nick Begich leads in Alaska’s US House race. Defend American Jobs, Fairshake’s Republican-facing affiliate, backed him with $508,142 in the August primary. The same PAC put $150,600 behind Rep. David Rouzer, who leads in North Carolina’s 7th District. Louisiana state Sen. Blake Miguez will face Democrat Chauna Banks in a Dec. 12 runoff for the state’s 6th District. The Fellowship PAC backed Miguez with $250,000. The Associated Press called the race in South Carolina’s 2nd District for incumbent Rep. Joe Wilson on the morning of Nov. 11. Stand With Crypto rates Wilson as “strongly supportive of crypto.” His win brought the group’s House tally to 246 crypto supporters and 107 opponents, while the Senate stood at 50 supporters and 33 opponents. In the remaining races, Stand With Crypto lists each candidate as either strongly supportive of crypto or having no stated position. “The new members that have no stance present an opportunity,” Blockchain Association Chief Policy Officer Lindsay Fraser told Cointelegraph. Educating the incoming congress Nearly one in four members of the incoming Congress will be new, Fraser said, and many have given little thought to blockchain technology. “To us, that represents a blank slate in terms of education,” she said. Blockchain Association is planning a January fly-in to reach newly elected lawmakers. “Leaving the 120th Congress with more members in that A and B category would be a huge success,” she said, referring to Stand With Crypto’s ratings. The group gives an A to candidates who strongly support crypto and a B to those who are somewhat supportive. Fraser said age plays a bigger role than party affiliation in how lawmakers vote on crypto. She said members under 55 are much more likely to support the industry and that the incoming class skews younger. Fraser said she wants the industry to enter the 2028 election “with two candidates who […] are thoughtful in regards to the industry,” so the sector can avoid “living and dying by the outcome of that election.” Magazine: Wall Street killed Bitcoin’s wild rallies: 10x’s Markus Thielen

news.summaryTr: Katar, Hürmüz Boğazı'ndaki krizin enerji, taşımacılık ve gıda fiyatları üzerinden küresel kalkınmayı tehdit ettiğini açıkladı. Doha, 2025'te BM ile 21 milyon dolarlık iki anlaşma imzalarken 2027'de yeni bir kalkınma toplantısına ev sahipliği yapacak.
news.articleText: Katar'dan Hürmüz uyarısı: Krizin küresel ekonomiye faturası ağırlaşıyor - Katar, Hürmüz Boğazı'ndaki krizin enerji, taşımacılık ve gıda fiyatları üzerinden küresel kalkınmayı tehdit ettiğini açıkladı. Doha, 2025'te BM ile 21 milyon dolarlık iki anlaşma imzalarken 2027'de yeni bir kalkınma toplantısına ev sahipliği yapacak. Katar, Hürmüz Boğazı'ndaki aksaklıkların enerji, deniz taşımacılığı ve gıda güvenliği üzerinden küresel ekonomiye etkilerinin giderek ağırlaştığı uyarısında bulundu. Katar Uluslararası İşbirliğinden Sorumlu Devlet Bakanı Meryem bint Ali el-Misned, krizin özellikle gelişmekte olan ülkelerin kalkınma kazanımlarını tehdit ettiğini söyledi. Hürmüz'deki kriz enerji ve gıda fiyatlarına yansıyor CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Misned, Paris Barış Forumu kapsamında Doha Forumu işbirliğiyle düzenlenen “Hürmüz Boğazı'nın Kapatılmasının Etkileri: Çatışmanın Küresel Kalkınmaya Gizli Maliyeti” başlıklı oturumda konuştu. Boğazdaki aksaklıkların yalnızca enerji piyasalarıyla sınırlı kalmadığını belirten Misned, etkilerin yakıt ve deniz taşımacılığından gübre ve gıda fiyatlarına, oradan da hane halklarının bütçelerine kadar yayıldığını ifade etti. Bölgesel krizlerin küresel sonuçlar doğurduğuna dikkat çeken Misned, uluslararası işbirliğinin güçlendirilmesi gerektiğini vurguladı. Diplomasi, egemenliğe ve uluslararası hukuka saygı ile seyrüsefer özgürlüğünün bölgesel istikrar ve küresel refah açısından temel unsurlar olduğunu söyledi. IMF'nin büyüme ve enflasyon tahminlerine dikkat çekti Misned, Uluslararası Para Fonu'nun (IMF) tahminlerini de gündeme getirdi. Buna göre gelişmekte olan ve yükselen ekonomilerde büyümenin geçen yılki yüzde 4,5 seviyesinden bu yıl yüzde 3,7'ye gerilemesi, küresel enflasyonun ise yüzde 4,7'ye yükselmesi bekleniyor. Bu rakamların arkasında artan yaşam maliyetleriyle mücadele eden aileler ve borç ödemeleriyle temel kamu hizmetlerinin finansmanı arasında zor tercihler yapmak zorunda kalan hükümetler bulunduğunu belirten Misned, krizin özellikle en fazla etkilenen ülkelerin yıllar içinde elde ettiği kalkınma kazanımlarını tehdit ettiğini kaydetti. Geçici bir krizin uzun vadeli kalkınma engeline dönüşmesinin önlenmesi gerektiğini vurguladı. Katar'dan BM ile 21 milyon dolarlık anlaşma Katar'ın krizlere karşı diplomasi ve kalkınma işbirliğini birlikte yürüttüğünü belirten Misned, ülkesinin 2025 yılında ilgili kurumları aracılığıyla Birleşmiş Milletler (BM) ile toplam 21 milyon dolar değerinde iki anlaşma imzaladığını hatırlattı. Anlaşmaların gıda güvenliği ve en az gelişmiş ülkelerin dayanıklılığının artırılması gibi alanları kapsayan Doha Eylem Programı'nı desteklemeyi amaçladığını söyledi. Misned, krizden en fazla etkilenen ülkelerin artan maliyetlerle mücadele edebilmesi için zamanında ve uygun koşullarda finansmana erişmesi gerektiğini belirterek bu süreçte borç yüklerinin daha da artırılmamasının önemine işaret etti. Doha, 2027'de en az gelişmiş ülkeleri ağırlayacak Katar, 25-27 Mart 2027 tarihlerinde Doha'da En Az Gelişmiş Ülkeler için Doha Eylem Programı'nın üst düzey ara dönem değerlendirme toplantısına ev sahipliği yapacak. Misned, toplantının uluslararası taahhütlerin somut sonuçlara dönüştürülmesi açısından önemli bir fırsat olacağını belirtti. “Mesajımız açıktır. Küresel krizlerin ortaya çıkmasında çok az sorumluluğu bulunan en az gelişmiş ülkeler, bu krizlerin sonuçlarından en fazla etkilenen ülkeler olmamalıdır” diyen Misned, erken harekete geçilmesi, koordinasyonun güçlendirilmesi ve kalkınma kazanımlarının korunması çağrısında bulundu. Katar'ın bu konudaki diyaloğu Aralık 2026'da düzenlenecek Doha Forumu'nda sürdürmesi bekleniyor.

IMF'nin büyüme ve enflasyon tahminlerine dikkat çekti Misned, Uluslararası Para Fonu'nun (IMF) tahminlerini de gündeme getirdi. Buna göre gelişmekte olan ve yükselen ekonomilerde büyümenin geçen yılki yüzde 4,5 seviyesinden bu yıl yüzde 3,7'ye gerilemesi, küresel enflasyonun ise yüzde 4,7'ye yükselmesi bekleniyor. Bu rakamların arkasında artan yaşam maliyetleriyle mücadele eden aileler ve borç ödemeleriyle temel kamu hizmetlerinin finansmanı arasında zor tercihler yapmak zorunda kalan hükümetler bulunduğunu belirten Misned, krizin özellikle en fazla etkilenen ülkelerin yıllar içinde elde ettiği kalkınma kazanımlarını tehdit ettiğini kaydetti. Geçici bir krizin uzun vadeli kalkınma engeline dönüşmesinin önlenmesi gerektiğini vurguladı. Katar'dan BM ile 21 milyon dolarlık anlaşma Katar'ın krizlere karşı diplomasi ve kalkınma işbirliğini birlikte yürüttüğünü belirten Misned, ülkesinin 2025 yılında ilgili kurumları aracılığıyla Birleşmiş Milletler (BM) ile toplam 21 milyon dolar değerinde iki anlaşma imzaladığını hatırlattı. Anlaşmaların gıda güvenliği ve en az gelişmiş ülkelerin dayanıklılığının artırılması gibi alanları kapsayan Doha Eylem Programı'nı desteklemeyi amaçladığını söyledi. Misned, krizden en fazla etkilenen ülkelerin artan maliyetlerle mücadele edebilmesi için zamanında ve uygun koşullarda finansmana erişmesi gerektiğini belirterek bu süreçte borç yüklerinin daha da artırılmamasının önemine işaret etti. Doha, 2027'de en az gelişmiş ülkeleri ağırlayacak Katar, 25-27 Mart 2027 tarihlerinde Doha'da En Az Gelişmiş Ülkeler için Doha Eylem Programı'nın üst düzey ara dönem değerlendirme toplantısına ev sahipliği yapacak. Misned, toplantının uluslararası taahhütlerin somut sonuçlara dönüştürülmesi açısından önemli bir fırsat olacağını belirtti. “Mesajımız açıktır. Küresel krizlerin ortaya çıkmasında çok az sorumluluğu bulunan en az gelişmiş ülkeler, bu krizlerin sonuçlarından en fazla etkilenen ülkeler olmamalıdır” diyen Misned, erken harekete geçilmesi, koordinasyonun güçlendirilmesi ve kalkınma kazanımlarının korunması çağrısında bulundu. Katar'ın bu konudaki diyaloğu Aralık 2026'da düzenlenecek Doha Forumu'nda sürdürmesi bekleniyor.

news.title: 'Not the answer': Labour MPs speak out against Rosebank as decision looms
news.summary: There is a growing expectation among senior Labour figures that drilling in the oil field will be given the green light.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: 'Not the answer': Labour MPs speak out against Rosebank as decision looms
news.summaryTr: There is a growing expectation among senior Labour figures that drilling in the oil field will be given the green light.
news.articleText: 'Not the answer': Labour MPs speak out against Rosebank as decision looms - Published Some Labour MPs have called on the government to reject the Rosebank oil field, saying it is "incompatible" with the UK's climate commitments. There is a growing expectation among senior Labour figures that drilling in the oil field off the north-west coast of Shetland will be given the go-ahead. Prime Minister Andy Burnham said on Wednesday that a decision would be "taken in due course" while Energy Secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh stressed that affordability of energy bills was her "overriding objective". But in a sign of the division within the party, more than a dozen Labour MPs expressed concerns in Parliament about approving it. Others expressed support, pointing to economic benefits. Supportive Labour MPs said some other parts of the world emitted far more greenhouse gases than the UK and warned of relying on imports. Reports have suggested that Chancellor John Healey is in favour of approval. Separately, it is understood some Labour backbenchers have organised a letter opposing Rosebank - intended for Burnham, but not yet sent - which more than 60 out of about 400 Labour MPs have indicated they support. One signatory told the BBC that approving Rosebank "would not create new jobs, would bring minimal money into the Treasury and be bad for the climate". "The government's central aim is to tackle the cost of living crisis, and drilling for more oil at Rosebank isn't the answer," the MP said. Wednesday's Westminster Hall - a type of parliamentary debate where backbench MPs raise topical issues but do not vote - was organised by Green MP Carla Denyer. Labour MP for Sheffield Central Abtisam Mohamed told the debate: "Rosebank fails on every test. "It will not benefit taxpayers who will shoulder the vast majority of the development costs, it will not strengthen our energy security because most of the oil will be sold on international markets, and it will not reduce energy bills for our constituents, who will remain exposed to volatile fossil fuel prices." Richard Burgon, a former frontbencher on the left of the party, said: "Rosebank is not compatible with our climate targets - it's dangerous to pretend otherwise." The UK is committed to reaching net zero by 2050 and wants to limit global warming to no more than 1.5C above the pre-industrial period. The UK government has always insisted that Rosebank is a quasi-judicial decision, formally resting with Fahnbulleh. She green-lit production in the Jackdaw gas field in the North Sea last month, but Rosebank hangs in the balance. Labour's manifesto upon entering power in 2024 pledged not to "issue new licences to explore new fields". Licences for both Jackdaw and Rosebank were granted by the then Conservative UK government in 2022 and 2023 respectively. But the Court of Session in Edinburgh ruled last year that the government had made the approvals unlawfully, leaving the current Labour government to make a fresh decision on whether to give the go-ahead. Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch sought to tease at Labour divisions on the issue during Prime Minister's Questions on Wednesday. Demand for fossil fuels During the debate, Labour MP Anna Gelderd said: "We live in an unprecedented era where our energy security is more vital than ever, in which jobs and wealth must be protected and economic opportunities seized - on both of these points, Rosebank fails." Labour MP Julia Buckley said she had received opposition to Rosebank from her constituents in "regularly flooded Shrewsbury" and said fossil fuels "belong in the past, not the future". She urged Fahnbulleh to "reject the oil licence in favour of renewables", adding: "Please don't add further to our climate emergency." Other Labour MPs expressed their support, including recently departed veterans minister Al Carns, who warned that Britain would continue to need fossil fuels for decades and importing more would be a mistake. "Refusing to produce it here does nothing on its own to eliminate that demand - it simply increases our reliance on imports which can carry their own environmental cost," he added. Those representing communities with ties to the oil and gas industry, including Jonathan Brash, the Labour MP for Hartlepool, stressed the benefits of approving Rosebank for British jobs. Speaking to BBC Radio 5 Live, Labour MP Bill Esterson, chair of Energy Security and Net Zero Committee, said "the economics of it (Rosebank) are that you should carry on with it" and "there's an element of energy security" by approving it. Energy minister Michael Shanks told the debate the government would take a "pragmatic approach" to a clean energy transition, stressing it was "not a turn off the taps government, but nor can we justifiably be a drill every last drop government either". news.title: Nomura explores sale of crypto unit Laser Digital: Bloomberg
news.summary: The potential sale of Laser Digital follows a fourth straight quarterly loss for Nomura’s European operations.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Nomura explores sale of crypto unit Laser Digital: Bloomberg
news.summaryTr: The potential sale of Laser Digital follows a fourth straight quarterly loss for Nomura’s European operations.
news.articleText: Nomura explores sale of crypto unit Laser Digital: Bloomberg The potential sale of Laser Digital follows a fourth straight quarterly loss for Nomura’s European operations. Japanese financial services giant Nomura Holdings is reportedly weighing a sale of its cryptocurrency subsidiary Laser Digital as Nomura’s European operations continue to post losses. Nomura has held talks with potential buyers, including Marex Group, Bloomberg reported Wednesday. The company has yet to make a final decision and could keep the business, according to the report. Nomura’s European businesses posted a pretax loss of 7.4 billion yen ($46.5 million) in the quarter ended Sept. 30, 2026, their fourth consecutive quarterly loss. The company posted pretax profits in every other reporting region over the same period. Nomura did not disclose whether Laser Digital, which is headquartered in Switzerland, contributed to the European result. Nomura is one of Japan’s largest financial services groups, with its investment management division overseeing 152.8 trillion yen ($960 billion) in assets as of September 2026. The potential sale comes less than three months after Laser Digital Japan secured the country’s first new crypto exchange license in four years, allowing the firm to expand its institutional crypto trading services in Japan. Established in 2022, Laser Digital provides institutional cryptocurrency trading, asset management and venture investment services. The company has also pursued expansion in the United States, receiving preliminary approval from the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency for its proposed national trust bank in May. During a January earnings call, chief financial officer Hiroyuki Moriuchi said the company would reduce its cryptocurrency trading positions to limit short-term volatility while continuing to expand Laser Digital over the medium to long term.
